<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:wang}
For every positive integer $n$ and every $A\in\Omega_n$, the following
inequality holds, with equality if and only if $A=J_n$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wang}
\operatorname{per}A\ge\operatorname{per}W_n(A).
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:bounds}
For every integer $n\ge2$ and every $A\in\Omega_n$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bounds}
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{per}A&\ge\gamma_n e^{a_n r^2},&
\operatorname{per}W_n(A)&\le\gamma_n(1+b_n r^2).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:centered}
For every integer $n\ge2$, every real $n\times n$ matrix $X$ with zero
margins and $\|X\|_{\rm op}\le1$, and every $2\le s\le n$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:centered}
|\sigma_s(X)|\le
\frac{\sigma_s(Q)}{n-1}\|X\|_F^2.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Let $n\ge2$. Theorem~\ref{thm:bounds} and $e^y\ge1+y$ give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{per}A-\operatorname{per}W_n(A)
&\ge\gamma_n\bigl(e^{a_nr^2}-1-b_nr^2\bigr)\\
&\ge\gamma_n(a_n-b_n)r^2,
\end{aligned}
\]
which proves~\eqref{eq:gap}. The comparison above gives $a_n>b_n$,
so the last expression is strictly positive when $A\ne J_n$. At
$A=J_n$, both permanents equal $\gamma_n$. For $n=1$, the only doubly
stochastic matrix is $A=J_1=[1]$; it is fixed by $W_1$, and both
permanents equal one. This proves~\eqref{eq:wang} and its equality claim.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
